blocks.text: Core Web Vitals describe loading, response to input and visual stability. Their short names are LCP, INP and CLS.

Use a local test page and browser developer tools. Code samples show a page choice or a measurement. Compare before and after under the same conditions; exact timings depend on the device and network.

blocks.code:
LCP: When the largest main content becomes visible.
INP: How quickly the page shows a response to interactions.
CLS: How much visible content unexpectedly moves.
blocks.title: Know the three web vital ideas

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: LCP is about the main content appearing, while INP is about responding to interaction.
CLS is separate: a page can load quickly and still move its controls unexpectedly.

blocks.text: The three measures help separate a slow load, a slow click response and a jumping layout.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: A single lab run is not the same as measurements from many real visits. Use each kind of evidence for its purpose.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Match a jumping button to the measure that tracks movement.
